findings.title: It was a matter of when, not if...
findings.summary_md: DIVD's initial public disclosure of its own breach, published roughly three days before the story's first_seen. The organization confirms it was hacked after almost seven years, states the modus operandi indicates an agentic AI powered attack, and says it is handling the case as worst-case-scenario and assume breach until proven otherwise. It blocked access to its infrastructure, started forensics with a third-party incident response team, reported the incident to the Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens and the National Cyber Security Centre, and discussed options with the police. The page itself carries no timestamp; published_at is the earliest Wayback Machine capture (2026-09-26 00:07 UTC), and the text promises the next public update on Monday 28 September.

findings.title: DIVD LinkedIn update: entry by technical vulnerability, not Citrix NetScaler
findings.summary_md: DIVD's Monday 28 September update on the incident. DIVD states it has a good idea of the entry path, exploitation of a technical vulnerability whose details are withheld to avoid interfering with the investigation or creating more victims, and confirms it was not Citrix NetScaler; it sees no link to known public threat actors and no involvement by a former volunteer. The update describes the agent deciding each next step itself, polluting its own MITM attack with password spraying, and over-explaining its comments, which eases reverse engineering, and thanks NCSC-NL, Merlon Security and NVISO Security for support. A next public update was promised for Thursday October 1. published_at is derived from the LinkedIn post ID, which encodes creation time in its high bits (2026-09-28 15:43 UTC, a Monday, matching the promised schedule).
